Facts in brief are that on 31.10.2017 at about 10.30 p.m. deceased was driving the motorcycle bearing no.DL- 5SBY-3818 and Vipin Kumar was pillion rider.
They were going from Delhi to Meerut for attending Jagran while taking all necessary precautions of traffic rules.

When motorcycle of deceased reached near Deepak Hoel, Partapur Byepass, Meerut suddenly a bus no.UP-15BT-1191 being driven by respondent no.1 rashly and negligently came from behind and hit the motorcycle with a great force.
Due to such impact deceased and pillion rider fell down on the road with motorcycle and deceased sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.
The pillion rider suffered multiple injuries and was taken to Pyare Lal Sharma Hospital, Meerut.
It is stated that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
It is stated that offending vehicle was owned by respondent no.2 and it was insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.

2. WS was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 wherein it is stated that no accident took place on the alleged date and time by bus no.UP- 15BT-1191 as accident took place by some unknown vehicle at the time when respondent no.1 was passing through the place of accident.
There was some crowd at the spot and people were asking for help.
Since respondent no.1 refused to help as it was medico legal matter, relatives of deceased stopped the bus forcibly and implicated the said bus in the present MACT No.71/2018 Page 2 accident.
It is stated that at the time of alleged accident respondent no.1 was employed as a driver on bus no.UP-15BT-1191 and was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
3. In the WS filed on behalf of respondent no.2 while denying the case of petitioners, it is stated that there was no negligence on the part of driver of bus.
It is stated that at the time of alleged accident bus no.UP- 15BT-1191 was insured with National Insurance Company Limited vide policy no.460700/31/17/6300000817 valid from 03.05.2017 to 02.05.2018.
It is stated that at the time of alleged accident respondent no.1 was employed as a driver on the said bus.
It is further stated that respondent no.2 has made no breach of any term and condition of insurance policy.

4. WS was also filed on behalf of respondent no.3/insurance company wherein objection has been taken that this Tribunal has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the present claim petition as this petition has been filed in Delhi only on the ground that petitioners are residents of Delhi however no document has been filed in support thereof.

It is stated that FIR was lodged on the next day of accident and same refers to accident having been caused by an unknown driver of offending vehicle.
Though it is stated that bus no.UP-15BT-1191 was insured with respondent no.3 during relevant period.
5. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor on 16.04.2018 :

(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no.UP-15BT-1191 on 31.10.2017 at about 10.30 PM at Near Deepak Hotel, Partapur Bye pass, Meerut, UP within the jurisdiction of PS Partapur, UP, in rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Suresh Kumar?

6. In order to substantiate their case petitioners have examined two witnesses.
PW1 is Smt.Usha Devi, widow of deceased; PW2 is Vipin, an eye witness.

Respondents have examined respondent no.1/R1W1 Mohit Kumar; R3W1 Sh.Ankit Malik, Junior Assistant, RTO Loni who proved documents of driving licence of respondent no.1; R3W2 is Ms.Rakesh Malhotra, Principal, Trinity Tiny Tots Play School who proved that deceased Suresh Kumar was working in their school as driver; R3W3 is Jagdish Prashad Sharma who is maternal uncle of deceased.
7. I have heard Sh.Upender Singh, ld. counsel for petitioner, Sh.S.D. Sharma, ld. counsel for respondent no.1 and 2 as well as Sh.S. Ghosh, ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
I have gone through their submissions and entire material available on record.
Issue No.1 8
. It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
MACT No.71/2018 Page 4 Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.

sentences.text: In order to establish the occurrence of accident, alleged rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1, on behalf of petitioners PW2 Vipin Kumar was examined who as per the case of the petitioners was pillion rider with the deceased on the motorcycle no.DL-5SBY-3818 of deceased.

PW2 Vipin deposed that on 31.10.2017 he along with Suresh s/o Dheer Singh was going toward Meerut from Delhi/Noida by motorcycle bearing no.DL-5SBY-3818 being driven by Suresh at a normal speed and correct side of road.

PW2 further deposed that at about 10.30 pm when they reached near Deepak Hotel, Moiuddinpur within the jurisdiction of PS Partapur, Meerut, in the meantime a bus registration no.UP-15BT-1191 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, rashly and negligently came from back side and hit the motorcycle with a great force.
As a result of which motorcycle fell down on the road due to which Suresh sustained grievous/fatal injuries.
PW2 further stated that accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle (respondent no.1).

10. Sh.Upender Singh, ld. counsel for petitioner submitted that testimony of PW2 coupled with criminal case record clearly establish that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.

It is submitted that since it came in the evidence of PW2 that offending vehicle no.UP-15BT-1191 had struck the motorcycle of the deceased from behind, therefore there was no question of any contributory negligence on the part of deceased.

Counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company submitted that it has been established on the record that deceased MACT No.71/2018 Page 5 was not having valid DL, when he was driving his motorcycle at the time of accident.

It is further submitted by counsel for the insurance that even upon going through the site plan prepared by UP Police in FIR No.747/2017, the site plan speaks for itself that accident had occurred due to contributory negligence of deceased when deceased tried to over take the bus no.UP-15BT-1191 and tried to take left turn in front of the bus and in that process accident occurred.

Much emphasis has been placed on site plan Ex.PW2/R3.
12.

contributory negligence cannot be attributed to deceased.
Counsel for the petitioner submits that police has charge sheeted the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no.1 in the criminal case.
Moreover PW2 in his cross examination has specifically stated that site plan is not correct.
On the question of deceased was not having DL at the time of accident, counsel has relied upon judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana vs. Surender Singh and ors. 2008 ACJ 1824.

sentences.text: 13. Having considered the submissions made at bar and the evidence on the record, first of all it be noted that as per the evidence of PW2 he was the pillion rider of the motorcycle being driven by deceased, MACT No.71/2018 Page 6 at the time of accident and PW2 himself suffered the injuries in the accident.
Evidence of PW2 appears to be cogent and specific regarding the manner in which accident has taken place.

PW2 has stated in specific terms that offending bus no.UP-15BT-1191,
struck the motorcycle of the deceased from behind and due to the impact deceased along with the motorcycle fell down on the road and sustained fatal injury.
PW2 further stated that he also sustained injuries.

PW2 was cross examined at length but his deposition remained consistent and specific regarding the manner in which accident took place as well as regarding the rash and negligent driving of bus no.UP-15BT-1191.

PW2 was duly confronted with the site plan prepared by the police in FIR No.747/2017 regarding which PW2 had stated that site plan Ex.PW2/R3 is not correct and witness reiterated that offending bus had hit their motorcycle from behind.
14.

As against this, if we examine the evidence of R1W1 (Mohit) who in his affidavit in examination in chief stated that he was driving bus no.UP-15BT-1191 and was coming from Meerut to Delhi and when he reached near Deepak Hotel Partapur, there was a crowd on the road and people was asking for help.
PW R1W1 further stated that there were school students in the bus therefore he refused for the help and therefore he was falsely implicated in the accident in question.

PW R1W1 further stated that he was driving his bus in a moderate speed and was having a valid DL.
15.
However in cross examination PW R1W1 admitted that FIR No.747/2017 at PS Partapur was registered against him for offence u/s 279, 338, 304 A IPC.

This witness further admits that offending bus no.UP- 15BT-1191 seized from the spot and that on the day of accident he left the said Usha Devi vs Mohit Lkumar on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147536752/
4 bus at the spot, after the accident and fled from the spot.
This witness further admitted that he had never filed any protest petition or any petition MACT No.71/2018 Page 7 regarding filing of charge sheet/FIR against him.
16. Thus reading the evidence of driver (PW R1W1) rather establish that he being involved in accident in question, has been charge sheeted by the local police in FIR No.747/2017.
Moreover driver admitted in his cross examination that he had left the offending bus at the spot of accident and fled away from there.

Thus in view of the testimony of PW R1W1 coupled with the criminal record documents including FIR, charge sheet, mechanical inspection report there is sufficient material available on the record to show that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.

In National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana and ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has laid down that certified copy of criminal court record including FIR,
recovery memo, mechanical inspection report regarding the accident are sufficient proof to reach to the conclusion that driver of the offending vehicle was negligent.

In the proceedings under M.V. Act,
no strict rule of evidence is required for proving rash and negligent driving.
17. No doubt in the site plan Ex.PW2/R3 indications made by the local police show the arrow of turning of the motorcycle of the deceased from left side in front of the bus.

However that site plan cannot be considered to be conclusive proof to establish contributory negligence, when even as per the case of the police in criminal documents it is nowhere stated that deceased was trying to over take the offending bus and in that process accident has been caused.
In this regard rather evidence of PW2 is cogent and specific as noted above.
18. The submissions regarding contributory negligence of the deceased, appears to be not supported with any evidence on the record.

It be noted that "contributory negligence" consists of the absence of that MACT No.71/2018 Page 8 ordinary care by injured/deceased in an accident which a person of ordinary prudence, ought to have taken for his own safety, and had it been exercised, would have enable him to avoid the injury of which he complains, or the doing of some act which he ought not to have done and but for which the calamity would not have occurred.

In Wakelin v. London and South Western Ry. Co. (1886) 12 AC 41 the basic principles of Contributory negligence in the field of accident under the Motor Vehicle Act is that when the defendants prove that the plaintiff has failed to take precautions against the possible danger and that those precautions, if taken, would have been effective to protect against the danger which occurred.

entities.text: Wakelin v. London and South Western Ry. Co. (1886) 12 AC 41
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. As such concept of contributory negligence would stand proved when there is positive evidence to show that complainant himself be a guilty of act or omission, which materially contributed to accident and result in an injury and damage.

For proof of contributory negligence, Tribunal must have to ensure that there is evidence proving injured contributing to incidence of accident, in other words evidence must establish that accident would not have occurred, but for negligence of injured also.

It be noted that contributory negligence cannot be inferred, rather must be established even if,
by preponderance of probability.
In this case merely because that deceased has not been proved to be holding a valid DL, ipso facto cannot be a reason to attribute contributory negligence to deceased.
Hon'ble Apex Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana's case (supra) has held that mere absence of driving licence with the deceased cannot be a fact to hold deceased guilty of contributory negligence.

Thus for the reasons stated above this Tribunal concludes that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no.UP-15BT-1191 being driven by respondent no.1.
MACT No.71/2018 Page 9  Issue No.2 21.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 22.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Suresh Kumar.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation) MACT No.71/2018 Page 11 The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
23.

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
24.
Petitioner no.1 Smt.Usga (PW1) in her evidence deposed that her deceased husband Suresh Kumar was aged about 42 years at the time of accident.

To prove this Usha Devi vs Mohit Lkumar on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147536752/
7 fact, she has proved on record post mortem report of deceased as Ex.PW1/2 and his Aadhar card as Ex.PW1/7.
Perusal of copy of Aadhar card of deceased Ex.PW1/7 shows that his date of birth is mentioned to be 01.02.1975.
As per this document, age of deceased on the date of his death was 42 years.
This document in the opinion of this Tribunal is conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of his death due to accident (31.10.2017) was 42 years.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
25.

Interesting aspect of the present matter is that petitioners have filed the present claim petition regarding the death of deceased in road side MACT No.71/2018 Page 12 accident, mentioning that deceased was a self employed and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month being a supplier of ready made garments.
In pleadings respondent no.3/insurance has denied it simpliciter.

However during the course of evidence respondent no.3 has examined R3W2 Rakesh Malhotra, Principal of Trinity Tiny Tots School of Noida and that witness stated that deceased was employed in that school and was being paid consolidated salary of Rs.12,000/- per month.

sentences.text: PW R3W2 though stated that salary record/register regarding deceased Suresh has been stolen by the thief and complaint in this regard was made to the local police.

However that witness has himself issued a certificate Ex.R3W2/4, wherein he has certified that deceased Suresh Kumar s/o Dhir Singh was employed in his school from 27.04.2017 till the date of accident i.e. 31.10.2017 and was drawing consolidated salary of Rs.12,000/-
per month.

26. It appears that such evidence was led on behalf of the insurance to disprove the claim of petitioners regarding earning of deceased to be of Rs.20,000/- per month as claimed in the claim petition.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner during the course of arguments submitted that insurance company has rather proved the income of the deceased.

27. Having considered the evidence of PW1 as well as PW R3W2 on the question of the income of the deceased, this Tribunal is of considered view that the factum of deceased drawing salary of Rs.12,000/-
per month at the time of accident has been proved by preponderance of probabilities on the basis of Ex.R3W2/4 proved by none else than the insurance company itself.
As such the income of the deceased is taken to be Rs.12,000/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:
28.
As held above, deceased was 42 years of age at the time of MACT No.71/2018 Page 13 accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:

Future Prospects:
30.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 MACT No.71/2018 Page 14 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

31. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 42 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (between age of 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
32. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :

sentences.text: Instant claim petition has been filed by four petitioners i.e. widow of deceased and children of deceased.
Since, the deceased was survived by four dependents, one-fourth of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:

34. In case of Pranay Sethi (supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

In view of pronouncement of Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra) and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram and others 2018 ACJ 2782 compensation awardable under conventional heads, namely, loss to estate,
loss of consortium and funeral expenses are to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

INTEREST ON AWARD 37.
Petitioners shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY 38.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is matter of record that the vehicle in question was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.

Therefore the amount of compensation is payable by respondent no.3/
insurance company to the petitioners.
Relief 39.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.21,18,000/- to the petitioners along with interest @

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
. It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Thus in view of the testimony of PW R1W1 coupled with the criminal record documents including FIR, charge sheet, mechanical inspection report there is sufficient material available on the record to show that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
In the proceedings under M.V. Act,
no strict rule of evidence is required for proving rash and negligent driving.
However that site plan cannot be considered to be conclusive proof to establish contributory negligence, when even as per the case of the police in criminal documents it is nowhere stated that deceased was trying to over take the offending bus and in that process accident has been caused.
19. As such concept of contributory negligence would stand proved when there is positive evidence to show that complainant himself be a guilty of act or omission, which materially contributed to accident and result in an injury and damage.
For proof of contributory negligence, Tribunal must have to ensure that there is evidence proving injured contributing to incidence of accident, in other words evidence must establish that accident would not have occurred, but for negligence of injured also.
It be noted that contributory negligence cannot be inferred, rather must be established even if,
by preponderance of probability.
In this case merely because that deceased has not been proved to be holding a valid DL, ipso facto cannot be a reason to attribute contributory negligence to deceased.

5 20.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
27. Having considered the evidence of PW1 as well as PW R3W2 on the question of the income of the deceased, this Tribunal is of considered view that the factum of deceased drawing salary of Rs.12,000/-
per month at the time of accident has been proved by preponderance of probabilities on the basis of Ex.R3W2/4 proved by none else than the insurance company itself.
As such the income of the deceased is taken to be Rs.12,000/- per month.
Application of Multiplier:
28.
As held above, deceased was 42 years of age at the time of MACT No.71/2018 Page 13 accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
31. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 42 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (between age of 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
32. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
